_comment: The agent writes here instead of guessing on anything ambiguous or hard-gated. Empty items = nothing blocking the builder.

items.summary: National geo architecture is BUILT (state > county > city > treatment; /{state}/{county}/{city}/{treatment}/ URLs + state/county/city hubs + sitemap.xml). It reads an OPERATOR-OWNED geo tree at config/thresholds.json -> seed_scope.geo. With no geo tree, it back-compat-builds the current flat 'neighborhoods' as active cities in Miami-Dade, FL. To activate new counties/cities, the operator adds them to seed_scope.geo with status active|planned (builder builds only 'active'; never edits config).
items.note: Each new active city still needs a prospector + ratings pass (per the density/pricing playbook) before it has real listings. Plan: builder/PLAN_geo_expansion_south_florida.md. State stays out of URLs only if single-state; national keeps /{state}/ as designed.
items.data_fields: Prospector clinic records may carry optional 'county' and 'state' slugs for disambiguation; 'neighborhood' is the city slug. addressRegion (state) belongs in schema.

items.summary: Information-gap handling is implemented, but the completeness thresholds are OPERATOR-OWNED and live in config/thresholds.json. The builder reads them and must never invent them — and cannot edit config/ (hard-gated). Until the operator adds the block, the new gate runs in DRY-RUN (reports only); it enforces nothing.
items.action: Add this block to config/thresholds.json to switch the gate from dry-run to enforced:

dry_run_findings_under_recommended_thres.empty_state_fields: 19/21 clinics have no email (Call-only), 3 have no phone, 66/70 listing-instances have no published price (-> 'request a quote').

items.note: Once the block is added, re-run the build to ENFORCE (those listings excluded, those 4 pages held). Adjust min_listings etc. to taste — it's your call.

items.summary: Each page now carries a short factual treatment-guidance blurb (builder/build.py -> TREATMENT_GUIDANCE), labeled 'general guidance only — not medical advice'. In a medical vertical this copy should get clinician/legal review before deploy.

Seed is built and committed to auto/build (18 rated pages + homepage + claim intake). Deploy is the separate, human-gated step (Vercel/Cloudflare) — the builder does not deploy. Claim-listing form is intake-only (routes to CRM on a deploy-time integration); the builder sends no outreach.
